fixes.title: Opening Edit Profile and pressing Save silently destroys the reducer and rewrites focal length / image scale by 25%
fixes.summary: The profile row encodes the optical train as a PAIR: telescope_focal_length is the OTA's native focal length and focal_length is the EFFECTIVE (post reducer/barlow) value that reaches the FITS FOCALLEN card, the plate-solve scale hint, the framing FOV and the guider px->arcsec conversion. Only the first-run wizard ever wrote the two apart. Edit Profile had a single 'Focal Length' box, seeded it from telescopeFocalLength in preference to focalLength (profile_editor_dialog.dart:208-213), and then wrote that one number back into BOTH columns plus focalRatio (profile_data_operations.dart:517,546-548) -- so a no-op open+save collapsed 440.0mm/f4.4 back to 550.0mm/f5.5. Fixed at the cause rather than by round-tripping the number: the editor now models the reducer explicitly. A 'Reducer / Barlow' field was added to the Optical Train section, seeded from the ratio the two stored columns already encode (focalLength / telescopeFocalLength -- the row has no reducer column, but the pair IS the reducer), bounded by the shared OpticalTrainLimits.min/maxReducerFactor window the wizard uses. Save writes the native value to the telescope columns and native x reducer to focalLength/focalRatio. Every derived readout (f/Ratio, Scale, and a new 'Effective FL' entry) now goes through the same effective focal length, so the preview can no longer claim an f-ratio the saved profile does not have; the computed-value Row became a Wrap so the third entry cannot overflow the 600px dialog. Two extra correctness items came with it, because without them the fix would only have relocated the defect: the effective product is rounded to 4dp because 550*0.8 == 440.00000000000006 in binary floats and would itself make a no-op save rewrite the row; and focalRatio is now null instead of a meaningless 0.0 when the focal length is unspecified (ProfileValidator.validateWireProfile rejects focalRatio <= 0, so the old value made a blank-optics profile unsavable over the remote POST path).
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/equipment/profile_editor_reducer_round_trip_test.dart -- 3 tests: (1) 'opening a reducer-equipped profile and saving with no edits leaves the stored optics untouched' seeds the exact wizard row (focal_length 440, telescope_focal_length 550, aperture 100, focal_ratio 4.4), asserts the reducer field reads 0.8 and the readout reads f/4.4 (not f/5.5), taps Save Changes with zero edits and re-reads the row; (2) 'a reducer typed into the editor is folded into the stored focal length'; (3) 'a barlow that pushes the train past the f-ratio ceiling is rejected rather than persisted'.
fixes.caveats: Fail-without-fix verified by reverting the effective-focal-length computation in _validateForm to the old 'write the typed focal length into both columns' behaviour: all 3 tests fail, tests 1 and 2 with exactly the reported symptom (Expected: <440.0>  Actual: <550.0>). Restored; the full skotiq_app equipment suite is 133/133 green (--exclude-tags golden; the 3 captures_landscape_test.dart failures are the host-specific golden baselines documented in that file's header and excluded from `melos run test` on Linux, and they render EquipmentScreen with no dialog open). Analyzer and dart format clean on every touched file. Reducer factors that are not exactly representable (e.g. a stored pair whose ratio is 1/3) are seeded rounded to 4 decimal places, so such a profile's focal length can shift by up to native*5e-5 mm on save -- negligible next to the 25% error it replaces, and no real reducer/barlow has such a factor.
fixes.needs_shared_change: 1) The Settings > Equipment Profiles INLINE profile editor (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/**, not my ownership) is the other surface that funnels through ProfileValidator and can collapse the same pair; it should get the same reducer field. 2) The reducer parser currently lives as a private helper in profile_data_operations.dart; its proper home is ProfileValidator.parseReducerFactor in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/equipment_profile_validation.dart alongside parseFocalLength/parseAperture, so both editors and the POST /api/profiles handler share one contract. Note equipment_profile_validation.dart:220-222 documents '_standInReducerFactor -- a profile row has no reducer field'; that is still true of the schema, but the ratio between the two focal-length columns is now load-bearing as the reducer, and validateWireProfile's telescope cross-check (lines 401-405) validates the two columns as independent trains rather than as native + effective.

fixes.title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected' against a host that does not exist
fixes.summary: PARTIAL AT THE ROOT, FULL AT THE SURFACE -- the true cause is one line in a file I do not own; see needs_shared_change. Cause: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102 (_discoverAddressDevices) catches the bridge's connection failure, logs a warning and returns const <DeviceInfo>[]. The Rust side is correct (api_discover_indi_at_address maps a refused socket to SkotiqError::connection_failed), so 'server up with no drivers loaded' and 'nothing is listening on that address' arrive at the dialog as the identical empty list, and the dialog's own catch branch is unreachable. What I fixed in my own file: the dialog no longer INFERS a connection from an empty device list. Only an actually-enumerated device proves the server answered, so `_statusSuccess` is now `devices.isNotEmpty`; an empty result renders with the failure icon and the message 'No INDI devices at <host>:<port>. If indiserver is running there, it has no drivers loaded - otherwise check the host and port.', which states exactly what the probe established and nothing more. This is deliberately NOT a replacement of one false claim with another: it does not assert the host is unreachable (the dialog cannot know that today), it withdraws the unsupported claim. The catch branch was also reworded to name the endpoint that was probed ('No response on <host>:<port>. $e'), mirroring the PHD2 test on the onboarding guider step, so it produces the precise socket error the moment the core swallow is removed.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/equipment/indi_server_dialog_test_connection_test.dart -- 3 tests: (1) 'an address that enumerates no devices is not reported as connected' (stub DeviceService returns [], asserts no 'Connected.' text, the No-INDI-devices message naming 192.0.2.77:7624, and the error icon rather than the success tick); (2) 'an address that enumerates a device is reported as connected' (the legitimate success path still shows the green tick); (3) 'a thrown probe names the endpoint it failed on' (covers the branch that becomes reachable once the core swallow is removed).
fixes.caveats: Fail-without-fix verified by reverting `_statusSuccess = n > 0` to the old unconditional `true`: test 1 fails with the exact live string -- Found 1 widget with text containing Connected.: Text("Connected. Found 0 devices."). Restored; all 3 pass. Because the core backend still swallows the socket failure, the message a user with a typo'd address sees today is the 'No INDI devices at ...' wording rather than the precise 'Connection refused'; that becomes the precise error automatically once the shared change below lands, with no further edit here.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102 -- `_discoverAddressDevices` must rethrow instead of returning `const <DeviceInfo>[]` after logging. Every existing caller already handles a throw and is currently WORSE off for the swallow: providers/unified_discovery_provider.dart:377-390 wraps the call in try/catch specifically to produce 'INDI server connection failed: $e' (that error string is dead code today, so a discovery sweep against a dead INDI server silently reports zero devices instead of a reachability error); apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/device_discovery_handlers.dart:211-220 catches and returns 500; and this dialog's catch is the branch tested above. The same swallow covers discoverAlpacaAtAddress, so Alpaca's address probe has the identical false-success shape.
